lessonInput.title: Functions and scope
lessonInput.objectives: Use only the supplied claims to make a defensible distinction without adding outside facts.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: A function is a named, reusable block of code defined with def that runs only when it is called; variables created inside it are local to that call. Claim 1: A function is defined with the def keyword, a name, parentheses, and a colon, with an indented body. Claim 2: A variable's scope is the part of the program where it can be accessed. Claim 3: A variable created inside a function has local scope and cannot be accessed outside the function. Claim 4: A variable created outside any function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.
lessonInput.readings: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §6.1 Defining functions; §6.3 Variable scope

claims: A function is a named, reusable block of code defined with def that runs only when it is called; variables created inside it are local to that call.
A function is defined with the def keyword, a name, parentheses, and a colon, with an indented body.
A variable's scope is the part of the program where it can be accessed.
A variable created inside a function has local scope and cannot be accessed outside the function.
A variable created outside any function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.

anchors.quote: A function is a named, reusable block of code that performs a task when called
A function is defined using the def keyword
A variable's scope is the part of a program where the variable can be accessed
A variable created within a function has local scope and only exists within the function
A variable created outside of a function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program

attribution: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §6.1 Defining functions; §6.3 Variable scope

facts: A function is a named, reusable block of code defined with def that runs only when it is called.

scenario.su: A programmer defines a function named process_data that calculates a total. Inside this function, a variable 'total' is created to store the result. The main program attempts to print the value of 'total' after the function call, but it results in an error.
scenario.ma: The programmer compares the function definition where 'total' is created with the line outside the function where 'total' is accessed to identify the scope violation.

facts: A function is a named, reusable block of code that runs only when called.
Variables created inside a function are local to that call and do not persist globally.
The def keyword introduces a function name, parentheses, and a colon before an indented body.
Variable scope is the part of a program where a variable can be accessed.
A variable created outside any function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere.

keyTerms.df: A function is a named block of code defined to be reused when called, not when written.
keyTerms.eg: A def block that prints a message only after a later call shows a function.
keyTerms.mi: Any indented code is automatically a function, even without def or a call.
keyTerms.cx: Indentation alone does not make a function; the defining marker and later call are both required.

keyTerms.df: Variable scope is the region of a program where a variable name can be accessed successfully.
keyTerms.eg: A name used inside one function but not outside it demonstrates limited variable scope.
keyTerms.mi: Scope means a variable changes value every time it is used in a program.
keyTerms.cx: Scope concerns where a name is reachable, not how often its value changes.

keyTerms.df: Global scope describes a variable created outside functions that remains accessible throughout the program.
keyTerms.eg: A name defined before any function and read inside another block shows global scope.
keyTerms.mi: A global variable can be accessed only inside the function where it was created.
keyTerms.cx: That reverses the idea of global scope; outside-function names are reachable across the program.

scenario.su: A debugging notebook shows a def block named score_total and a later print statement that uses score. The notebook also notes that score is created inside the function, while limit is created before the function, and the team must choose which name a later line can read without changing the code.
scenario.ma: Compare the function header with its indented body, the note beside score saying 'created inside', and the separate line where limit is defined before def. Decide which name can be accessed later outside the function while the other stays limited to one call.

mc.q: A script shows a def line with parentheses and a colon, followed by an indented block. Which statement best matches how that structure behaves compared with the code above it?
op: It defines a reusable function that runs only after a later call.
It copies the indented code into every earlier line automatically.
It creates a global variable that is available immediately everywhere.
It makes every line in the file run only inside that block.
mc.ex: The defining pattern is a named block that waits until called, while the nearby distractor confuses definition with immediate execution.

mc.q: After a call finishes, a name assigned inside the function is read on a later line and raises a lookup problem. Which explanation best fits the displayed behavior?
op: The name has global scope because it was created during execution.
The name has local scope inside that call and is not available outside it.
The indented block automatically promotes every name to program-wide access.
The function definition erased the name before the body started.
mc.ex: The assignment inside the function creates a local name for that call only; the nearby distractor wrongly treats creation during execution as global access.
